item: The OSM CLI loops and comprehensions under a cleanup finally keep their back-edge inside the try (R163)
summary: ingest_country's per-object loop and reference_run._run's per-phase loop ended in a bare if, so on CPython 3.13 their back-edge sat outside the exception table of the try whose finally closes the location store / deletes the throwaway store; an interrupt there skipped the cleanup. Each loop's last statement is now a guard clause (same body, same behaviour). The review of the final head found the same class in two comprehensions inside the same try bodies (the location filter in ingest_country, the environment copy in _run; measured on 3.13: 12,283 of 12,491 interrupts in a minimal try/finally around such a comprehension skipped the finally), which are now small functions of their own (_present, _inherited_environment). tests/test_r163_osm_loops.py reads the compiled code with the dis helper of test_gates_survive_an_interrupt.py, fails for ANY uncovered loop head in the two functions except the comprehensions of _run's own finally body (where a skipped remainder is the same either way), and checks that the watched loop heads still exist; it is red with the old code (2 failed on origin/main's src/osm). Also: tests/test_briefing_shared_files.py::test_two_processes_recording_reasons_lose_no_reason failed once in the core-only CI job on this PR (parent-1001 in the message): the reasons store keeps the newest 1,000 by design and the test's parent loop ran until the child exited, so a slow child startup let the parent write past the cap and its own oldest reasons were trimmed. The parent now stops 40 short of the cap (the child writes 40); nothing is retried.
